title: Chicken Scarpariello
subtitle: Braised chicken thighs with sausage, peppers and cherry peppers
excerpt: Bone-in chicken thighs and Italian sausage braised in white wine with jarred cherry peppers. Sweet, sharp and savoury all at once. A loud, satisfying one-pan supper.
sourceNotes: Italian-American tradition, popularised in New York and New Jersey. Synthesised from multiple restaurant and home cook sources.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The braise improves overnight. Reheat gently on the hob.

content.text: Chicken scarpariello is a brash Italian-American braise. Chicken and sausage cook together with white wine and pickled cherry peppers. Keep the heat steady so the chicken skin stays crisp on the bottom before the liquid goes in.

items.prepNote: from a jar, roughly chopped, plus 3 tbsp brine

content.text: Season the chicken thighs well with salt and black pepper on both sides.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium-high heat. Place the chicken skin-side down and cook for 8 minutes without moving. Turn and cook for 3 more minutes. Remove to a plate.
Add the sausage pieces to the same pan. Brown them on all sides for about 5 minutes. Remove to the plate with the chicken.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the peppers and garlic to the pan. Cook for 4 minutes until the peppers soften slightly.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Add the stock, pepper brine, cherry peppers and rosemary.
Nestle the chicken and sausage back into the pan. Cover and cook on a low heat for 20 minutes.
Remove the lid and cook for a further 5 minutes to reduce the sauce slightly. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.cause: The chicken was not dried before cooking, or the pan was not hot enough.
items.fix: Pat the skin very dry and make sure the oil is hot before the chicken goes in. Do not move it.

items.cause: Too much pepper brine or the wine was very acidic.
items.fix: Stir in a small knob of butter at the end. It rounds the edge off quickly.

items.cause: It was overcooked in the browning stage.
items.fix: Brown the sausage quickly on high heat. It finishes cooking in the braising liquid.
